record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let f be analytic on D and suppose that integral_D h(z)|f(z)|^2 dS(z) <= h(0) for every positive bounded harmonic function h on D. Must f be the normal limit, meaning uniform convergence on compact subsets of D, of finite zero divisors for the Bergman space?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 6.2 Suppose f is analytic on D

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $dS$ denote normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. For a finite set $Z=\{z_1,\dots,z_n\}\subset\mathbb{D}$ (with multiplicities allowed), the canonical (contractive) zero-divisor for the Bergman space $A^2(\mathbb{D})$ associated with $Z$ is the unique function $G_Z\in A^2(\mathbb{D})$ vanishing exactly on $Z$ such that $\|G_Z\|_{A^2}=1$ and $\|f/G_Z\|_{A^2}\le\|f\|_{A^2}$ for every $f\in A^2(\mathbb{D})$ that vanishes on $Z$; equivalently, $G_Z$ is the extremal solution of the corresponding extremal problem. Call any such $G_Z$ a finite zero-divisor.

Suppose $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ is analytic and satisfies
$$\int_{\mathbb{D}} h(z)\,|f(z)|^2\,dS(z)\ \le\ h(0)$$
for every positive bounded harmonic function $h$ on $\mathbb{D}$.

Must $f$ be a normal limit of finite zero-divisors? That is, must there exist a sequence $\{G_{Z_n}\}$ of finite zero-divisors for $A^2(\mathbb{D})$ such that $G_{Z_n}\to f$ uniformly on every compact subset of $\mathbb{D}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up extensive literature on contractive zero-divisors and extremal functions in Bergman spaces (Hedenmalm; Duren–Khavinson–Shapiro–Sundberg; Aleman–Richter–Sundberg's Beurling-type theorem) and on Korenblum's principle, but no source was found that explicitly confirms or refutes this specific Carathéodory-type characterization: that the harmonic-majorant inequality $\int_{\mathbb{D}}h|f|^2\,dS\le h(0)$ for all positive bounded harmonic $h$ forces $f$ to be a normal limit of finite Bergman zero-divisors. The current status from public sources is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Contractive zero-divisors in Bergman spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and properties of canonical contractive zero-divisors in A^p, generalizing Hedenmalm's result for p=2.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework of finite contractive zero-divisors in Bergman spaces but does not address the Carathéodory-type normal-limit characterization.

status_evidence.title: Beurling's Theorem for the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Aleman–Richter–Sundberg characterize invariant subspaces of the Bergman shift via wandering subspaces and contractive divisors.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural result for Bergman zero-divisors but does not explicitly resolve the stated conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on Bergman-space zero-divisors and extremal functions.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture appears as an open problem in this survey context.
